claims.sentence: In an annotated corpus of 3,063 citations to 100 highly cited biomedical articles, about 39\% contained an accuracy error \citep{sarol2024citationintegrity}.
claims.claim: Corpus of 3,063 annotated citations to 100 highly cited biomedical articles; ~39% had accuracy errors.
claims.excerpt: We manually annotated 100 highly-cited biomedical publications (reference articles) and citations to them. ... A total of 3063 citation instances were annotated (39.18% with accuracy errors).

claims.sentence: On human-annotated biomedical citations, the authors' best-performing model reached 0.59 micro-F1 and 0.52 macro-F1 \citep{sarol2024citationintegrity}.
claims.claim: The authors' best-performing model on their human-annotated biomedical citation corpus reached 0.59 micro-F1 and 0.52 macro-F1.
claims.excerpt: The best performing model—which uses citation sentences as citation context, the BM25 model with MonoT5 reranker for retrieving top-20 sentences, and a fine-tuned MultiVerS model for accuracy label classification—yielded 0.59 micro-F1 and 0.52 macro-F1 score.
claims.location: p. 1, Abstract (Results); see also Sec. 3, Table 4 (p. 6)
claims.note: Supported. Context only: oracle variants given gold evidence reach 0.73-0.75 micro-F1 and GPT-4 in-context learning reaches 0.65 micro-F1 (0.45 macro-F1); 'best-performing' is the authors' own label for the end-to-end model, so the wording is accurate.
